question: Which two properties of carbon are mainly responsible for the formation of a large number of carbon compounds?

options.text: Tendency to form ionic bonds and lose electrons
High atomic mass and large atomic size

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tetravalency and catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique property of **carbon** atoms to form **covalent bonds** with other **carbon** atoms, resulting in long chains, branched chains, or closed rings. This ability is due to the very strong **carbon-carbon** bond energy. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct regarding catenation.***
 
• **Tetravalency** refers to the fact that **carbon** has **4** valence electrons in its outermost shell. This allows a single **carbon** atom to form four chemical bonds with other atoms like **hydrogen**, **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, or **sulfur**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct regarding tetravalency.***
 
• The **small size** of the **carbon** atom allows its nucleus to hold the shared pairs of electrons strongly. This results in the formation of exceptionally stable and strong bonds, which is a major factor in the existence of a vast number of **carbon compounds**.
 
• **Carbon** primarily forms **covalent bonds** rather than **ionic bonds**. This is because **carbon** has **4** electrons in its valence shell, and losing or gaining **4** electrons would require a massive amount of energy. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon** is a **non-metal** and has a relatively **low atomic mass** of **12** and a **small atomic size**. These properties are opposite to what is suggested in some incorrect options. ***Hence, statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organic Chemistry**: This is the dedicated branch of chemistry that deals with the study of **carbon** and its compounds. Today, millions of **organic compounds** are known to scientists, far exceeding the number of compounds formed by all other elements combined.
 
• **Isomerism**: Due to its unique bonding capabilities, **carbon** compounds often exhibit **isomerism**, where molecules have the same chemical formula but different structural arrangements, further increasing the diversity of **carbon** structures.
 
• **Atomic Properties**: **Carbon** has the **atomic number 6** and its **electronic configuration** is **2, 4**. It belongs to **Group 14** and **Period 2** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**: **Carbon** exists in various forms in nature called **allotropes**. The most common ones include **Diamond** (the hardest natural substance), **Graphite** (a good conductor of electricity), and **Buckminsterfullerene** (a spherical molecule with **60** carbon atoms).
 
• **Functional Groups**: **Carbon** chains can be attached to various **functional groups** such as **alcohol (-OH)**, **aldehyde (-CHO)**, **carboxylic acid (-COOH)**, and **ketones (>C=O)**, which determine the chemical properties of the resulting **organic compounds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **C-C bond energy** is approximately **348 kJ/mol**, which is significantly higher compared to other elements like **Silicon** (approx. **297 kJ/mol**), explaining why **carbon** shows the highest degree of **catenation**.
 
• **Hydrocarbons** are the simplest **carbon** compounds, consisting only of **carbon** and **hydrogen**. They are classified into **Saturated** (alkanes) and **Unsaturated** (alkenes and alkynes) based on the presence of single, double, or triple bonds.
 
• In **2024**, **carbon** remains the backbone of life and **biotechnology**, as it is found in **DNA**, **proteins**, **carbohydrates**, and **fats**.
</ul
